extracted.intended_audience: fact-checking organizations, journalists, researchers, donors, and members of the public interested in IFCN transparency
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-level transparency statement explaining how the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) meets the IFCN Code of Principles: legal structure, published work, nonpartisanship, funding disclosure, organizational/contact details, methodology, and corrections. Intended to document IFCN's compliance and disclosure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal structure (criterion 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Fact-Checking Network is a business unit of the Poynter Institute for Media Studies, a nonprofit journalism training institution. Poynter is registered as a 501(c)(3). Poynter is also the nonprofit owner of The Tampa Bay Times. The Director of the International Fact-Checking Network and all its staff are employees of the Poynter Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN staff choose to avail themselves of the advice of fact-checkers around the world through several means, the most important of which is the IFCN Advisory Board with a consultative role. The statement situates IFCN within Poynter’s legal/nonprofit framework to disclose organizational relationships that could bear on independence or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published work (criterion 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFCN has a dedicated section on the Poynter website where we cover trends, formats, and news regarding fact-checking, “fake news” and misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-facing content and coverage of fact-checking work is centralized on Poynter.org/ifcn; this documents where IFCN’s outputs and reporting about fact-checking activity can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisanship (criterion 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFCN does not take sides in any policy discussion beyond access to information and fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN staffers cannot be members of political parties nor publicly support candidates for elected office. This rule is presented as a safeguard to maintain neutrality in policy discussions and public political activity by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of funding (criterion 4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The major donors of The Poynter Institute are listed; tax filings are available. From its launch in 2015, the IFCN has received funding from multiple named organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists specific funders (Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation, Duke Reporters’ Lab, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Google, Facebook/Meta, U.S. State Department, National Endowment for Democracy, Omidyar Network (Luminate), Open Society Foundations, Fritt Ord Foundation, Craig Newmark Philanthropies, Park Foundation, etc.). IFCN has started to disclose income and expense statements beginning in 2019 and will publish annual statements at poynter.org/ifcn; verified signatories (starting 2022) will receive updates with details on donors and funding amounts for projects as they are announced. This criterion documents sources of financial support and ongoing financial disclosure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of organization / contact details (criteria 4b, 4c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff composition and advisory/organizational governance are disclosed: current staff (Director Angie Drobnic Holan; International Training Project Manager Alanna Dvorak; Community and Impact Manager Enock Nyariki; Code of Principles Program Manager Salvador Rodriguez-Ruiz) and information about the Advisory Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Board history and governance details are provided: established December 2016, term renewal December 2017 ratified by verified signatories; board members who resign/leave are replaced by a simple majority vote of remaining Board members plus the IFCN Director; the Advisory Board’s principal role is to help oversee the verification process of the code and it is consulted on other international/strategic decisions; bylaws enacted in 2020 and updated 2024 (link provided); Advisory Board members are unpaid; Poynter’s President holds an ex-officio independent seat (currently Neil Brown); independent advisory board members are invited by the IFCN Director and appointed only if approved by a 2/3 majority of the board; independent members do not cast votes for incoming applications to IFCN’s Code of Principles but participate in other discussions. The guidance documents how organizational roles, appointment, voting, and bylaws operate to support transparency about governance and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (criterion 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete list of IFCN activities is available; IFCN staff are governed by the Poynter Institute’s ethics policy; the process to apply to be verified as a signatory of the Code of Principles is explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN staff may help surface common positions among fact-checkers and, after consultation among verified signatories and key actors, may advocate for those positions with third parties—while always making clear which organizations it does or doesn’t speak for. Example: coordinated an open letter to Mark Zuckerberg in November 2016. Links are provided to activities and the verification application process. This criterion documents procedures, decision-making practices, and how IFCN interacts with the broader fact-checking community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections (criterion 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: IFCN follows Poynter’s corrections policy for its articles and directs readers to where corrections can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to Poynter’s corrections policy. It also links State of the Fact-Checkers reports for 2018–2024 and notes that starting from 2020 IFCN publishes annual transparency reports on its Code of Principles (with the 2020 report downloadable). This documents correction practices and historical transparency reporting.
